articles.title: The best robot vacuum and mop to buy right now
articles.summary: Roborock, Narwal, and Dreame bots top our list of the best robot vacuums that are also excellent at mopping your floors.
articles.body: Robot vacuums that can both mop and sweep your floors have improved significantly in recent years. While they are still not as effective as good ol’ manual labor, if you run them regularly, they will help keep your floors cleaner with much less effort on your part. The difference is that newer “combo” robot vacuum-and-mop models are designed to actually scrub your floors. The first robot vacuums that could also “mop” simply slapped a thin, flat microfiber pad on the bot that kind of Swiffer-ed your floor. Basically, all this was good for was getting up fine dirt that the vacuum left behind. Today’s models come with vibrating or oscillating mop pads or roller mops. Most have onboard water tanks to keep the mops wet while in use, and many can wash and dry their mops in their charging docks, which also automatically empty and refill their water tanks, meaning less work for you. While most robot vacuums today have some sort of mopping feature, this guide focuses on those that excel at mopping. If you’re more interested in the best vacuum, check out my guide to floor-sweeping bots. The downside to these combo bots with serious mopping chops is that they tend to be bigger and heavier and need more frequent intervention than regular vacuum bots. Water equals gunk, and cleaning their giant multifunction docks, even the self-cleaning ones, can be an icky job. You also have to empty and refill their tanks about once a week. Mopping bots also need to return to their docks more frequently than robot vacuums in order to refill their onboard water tanks. This means they’ll take longer to clean your floors than a dedicated vacuuming model, but they are doing two jobs at once. Robot mops with roller mops will self-clean as they work, negating this issue, but these models are also the biggest and bulkiest, as they carry a larger water tank. Combo bots can mop and vacuum simultaneously, but for especially dirty floors, it’s best to have the option to vacuum first and then mop. A mop-only mode is also good, as you can send the bot to clean up a wet spill without it sucking up water — something they’re not designed to do yet. If you have a lot of hardwood or tile floors and constantly struggle with muddy paw prints or the general dirtiness of life with multiple pets, people, and kids, a good robot vacuum-and-mop combo will definitely make your life easier. Featured Products Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow Narwal Flow Roborock Q10 S5 Plus Best mopping robot vacuum [Product: Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow | Multifunction dock: Yes / Mapping: Yes, lidar / AI-powered obstacle detection: Yes / Suction power: 20,000Pa / Remote check-in: Yes / Brush style: Single, rubber / Mop style: Roller mop / Mop lift: Yes, 15mm, with a shield / Mop washing: Yes, with hot water and warm air drying / Edge cleaning: Mop extension / Works with: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Matter My top picks for the best robot vacuum — the Matic and Roborock Saros 10 — are both excellent mopping bots as well as vacuums. But, if you are looking for a robot vacuum that excels at mopping, then Roborock’s new Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is my top recommendation. Roborock’s first robot vacuum with a roller mop, the Curv 2 Flow’s features a new “SpiraFlow” cleaning system that demolished all my mopping tests. Roborock may be a bit late to the roller-mop game, but it brought the goods. The Flow is also a terrific vacuum with 20,000Pa of suction, and you get all of this for $999 — most top bots in this category cost well over $1,000. [Image: The roller mop on the Flow is both long and wide. Roborock’s VibraRise system (a flat mopping pad that vibrates to simulate scrubbing) has long been its signature wet-floor cleaning solution, and it’s one I think works very well. But it is slow. The new roller mop on the Flow gives you a much faster deep clean than the flat pad method (which is on the Saros 10). At almost 11 inches, the mop is also one of the longest I’ve tested, plus it extends outward to reach along baseboards and edges of furniture. It self-cleans as it works, and a built-in scraper squeegees away the dirty water. It uses an impressive 15 newtons (about 3.3 pounds) of downward pressure that made quick work of my dried-on ketchup test. The Flow did a great job of automatically detecting carpets and deploying its retracting mop cover, and it can also identify both hardwood and tile, as well as adjust cleaning strategies. When it spotted my spilled OJ test, it automatically switched to mop-only mode to avoid sucking the sticky juice into its bin. Its single DuoDivide brush does a good job on carpet and hardwood floors, and the unique design prevents hair tangles by funneling hair into the center, where it is sucked into the bin. [Image: [Image: [Image: I’m a big fan of the Qrevo Curv dock, which, as the name implies, features a curved design that looks more attractive in an open-plan space than the boxy docks that come with most robot vacs. It’s compact yet still has enough room for large water tanks and a disposable dust bag. The dock also features removable parts for easy cleaning, which is key to keeping these docks from getting grungy. The lidar-based navigation on the Curv 2 Flow is very good, although, as with all roller mop bots I’ve tested, it struggled to get into and out of tighter spaces. This is because they’re heavier and bulkier than non-roller mop bots, as they have to carry a larger onboard water tank and make room for that big mop. It was able to lift itself up slightly to navigate my high-pile, large-tassel living room carpet, something other roller-mop bots have struggled with. Obstacle avoidance is on par with that of a midrange vacuum. It has Roborock’s Reactive AI, which uses a camera and structured light to detect and avoid up to 200 obstacles as small as 3cm high and 5cm wide, according to the company. It did a good job dodging socks, shoes, and pet toys, but it did get tripped up by the occasional cable. If you want top-notch detection, you’ll need to bump up to the Saros 10. Best robot vacuum and mop for a mix of hard floors and rugs [Product: Multifunction dock: Yes / Mapping: Yes, lidar / AI-powered obstacle detection: Yes / Suction power: 20,000Pa / Remote check-in: Yes / Brush style: Dual rubber / Mop style: Dual spinning / Mop lift: Yes, 20mm, plus automatic removal / Mop washing: Yes / Edge cleaning: Mop extension / Works with: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Matter If you have a lot of fluffy rugs or carpets as well as hard floors, the Dreame X50 Ultra is the best robot vacuum and mop for you. It’s not quite as good at mopping as my top pick, but it’s better suited for high-pile carpet and rugs because it can automatically drop and reattach its spinning mopping pads during vacuuming. This means it becomes a vacuum-only bot when tackling carpets, without the hindrance of carrying a large roller mop or water tank. It’s also more agile and better at handling fluffy rugs and carpets. The big upgrade on the X50 compared to the X40 Ultra (a previous pick) is the addition of a “motorized swing arm” that functions like a leg, which allows it to maneuver over higher thresholds (up to 6cm). This new mechanism means it can get into more spaces — like over the high transition from my bedroom into my bathroom — and more easily tackle obstacles such as high-pile rugs. [Image: The Dreame’s wheels can lift up using two “legs” to get over small steps and high transitions between rooms. It also has higher suction power and a much-improved brush system that uses dual rubber rollers. It did an excellent job in my oatmeal-on-carpet tests, sucking up every last flake. The X50 maintains the X40’s excellent mopping capabilities, including the ability to automatically extend its mop pads and swing them to reach under your cabinets and consoles, letting it get further than even the longest extendable roller mop. Its new, retractable lidar tower also helps it reach under lower furniture. Obstacle detection is powered by a camera and structured light, and did okay in testing, although it did suck up the occasional sock. The downside of Dreame vacuums is the app, which frequently crashes and can take a while to load. When it works, however, it offers plenty of features and customization options to tailor your cleaning to your home. Best robot vacuum and mop for hard floors [Product: Narwal Flow | Multifunction dock: Yes / Mop style: Roller mop / Mop washing: Yes, hot water and hot air drying / Mop lift: Yes, 12mm / Edge cleaning: Yes / Mapping: Yes, lidar / AI-powered obstacle detection: Yes / Suction power: 22,000Pa / Vacuum brush style: Single, conical rubber bristle hybrid / Works with: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Siri Shortcuts Narwal has consistently had the best mopping bots in my testing, though most have sacrificed vacuuming for mopping prowess. The Flow is one of the first bots from Narwal that does both really well, even if the mop is still the star. The company’s first model with a self-cleaning roller mop, the Flow’s flat, wide-track-style mop has more surface area than any of the other bots I tested and passed all my mopping tests with flying colors. Wider than Roborock’s Curv 2 Flow mop and as long, it can also extend to reach into corners and along baseboards. It did very well in my mopping tests, even getting up the dried ketchup from tile grout. I like that the Flow can recognize various floor materials (tile, hardwood, marble, etc.), clean in the direction of the flooring, and automatically adjust its pressure and “mopping humidity” based on the floor type. It uses higher humidity on tile floors than on wood floors, which can be impacted by excessive moisture. [Image: [Image: As mentioned, vacuuming is much improved over some of Narwal’s previous models, with 22,000Pa of suction power and an excellent cone-style anti-tangle brush roll that rarely gets wrapped in hair. Its obstacle detection is great, too, and relies on a dual-camera system to identify and avoid obstacles. It also has a handy dirt detection feature that makes the bot go back and forth over a stain or dirty area to ensure it’s cleaned. However, navigation on Narwal’s previous robots has been spotty, and the new tower-less lidar here hasn’t improved things. While it means the bot is slimmer and can get under lower furniture, it did get confused and stuck a few times during testing. The Narwal also doesn’t handle high-pile rugs well, as there’s still only a 12mm mop lift and no mop cover, but you can set it to skip carpets entirely. My biggest problem with the Flow is one that plagued prior models: the Narwal app. It’s not easy to navigate, gets hung up between screens, and frequently disconnects from the robot. I love that Narwal also offers the option to use a dock that connects to your plumbing, which eliminates the chore of emptying and refilling the robot’s water tanks. Best budget robot vacuum and mop [Product: Roborock Q10 S5 Plus | Multifunction dock: No, auto-empty only / Mop style: Vibrating flat pad / Mop washing: No / Mop lift: Yes, 8mm / Edge cleaning: No / Mapping: Yes, lidar / AI-powered obstacle detection: Yes / Suction power: 10,000Pa / Brush style: Single bristle / rubber hybrid / Works with: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Siri Shortcuts Roborock’s Q10 S5 Plus is a budget robot with flagship features, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, automatic carpet detection, and support for Roborock’s fantastic app. It uses Roborock’s excellent VibraRise vibrating mopping system that actually scrubs your floors, and it can lift its mop up to 8mm to pass over low-pile carpets. All this can be had for under $400, at least when it’s on sale. [Image: [Image: There’s no multifunction dock, so you need to manually fill its onboard water tank (which is integrated with its bin), but it does come with a compact auto-empty dock. If you can handle emptying its large onboard bin yourself, you can ditch the dock and pick up the Q10 S5 for even less. Its lidar-based mapping and navigation system did a good job. Plus, using the excellent Roborock app, you can set specific rooms to clean, create no-go zones, and customize cleaning methods — including how it mops — features few bots in this price range offer. Other robot vacuum / mops to consider * My previous top pick in this guide, the $1,099.99 Ecovacs Deebot X8 Pro Omni, is an excellent robot mop with an extendable mop that can lift slightly over carpets. It has 18,000Pa suction and uses lidar and cameras for navigation and obstacle detection. Its multifunction dock is attractive and easy to use, but it doesn’t have a retractable mop cover, and its roller is much shorter than the Qrevo Curv 2 Flow’s. * Another previous pick, Narwal’s $1,499.99 Freo Z Ultra, is a mopping bot with dual spinning pads and a fluffy side brush to polish your baseboards. Its triangular spinning mop pads are particularly effective on tile grout, making this a good option for tile floors. It has 12,000Pa of suction power and a sleek-looking multifunction dock. * The $899.99 Eufy X10 Pro Omni, a previous pick, is a terrific budget option that features a multifunction dock that can wash its mop and drain and refill its water tank. It features 8,000Pa of suction power and has good obstacle detection for this price range. * The $1,499.99 Ecovacs X11 OmniCyclone is a bagless robot vac that features a roller mop and an impressive 19,500Pa of suction. It comes with a multifunction dock, and its mop can reach into corners. It handles floor transitions well, thanks to mechanical climbing levers. It also features a bagless auto-empty dock. * SharkNinja’s $999.99 PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro 2-in-1 robot vacuum mop can lift itself up as high as 20mm to get over rugs and transitions. Its automatic empty /wash / dry cleaning station doesn’t require bags, either. What we’re testing next * The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai Robot comes with a multifunctional dock, along with a self-cleaning roller mop, lidar navigation, and onboard cameras that can detect stains and clean accordingly. The company has yet to announce a price or release date, though you can read our hands-on for more details. * The $1,599.99 Dreame Aqua10 Ultra Roller Complete features a roller-style mopping system that continuously cleans itself in real time. Its companion model, the Aqua10 Ultra Track Complete, adds hot-water mopping and automatically adds cleaning solution as it moves, so you don’t have to stop and refill anything. * The $1,799.99 Dreame Matrix 10 Ultra comes with a multi-mop switching dock, one that lets it automatically swap between nylon scrub pads, sponge pads, and thermal mop pads based on where it’s cleaning. Its three-solution compartment also holds separate cleaners aimed at tackling pet odors, wood floors, and general messes, which the robovac will dispense on its own depending on the situation. Photography by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge Update, January 30th: Adjusted pricing / availability and added several new picks, including Roborock’s new Qrevo Curv 2 Flow, the Dreame X50 Ultra, the Narwal Flow, and Roborock’s Q10 S5 Plus. Sheena Vasani also contributed to this post.

articles.title: Google’s Gemini is now on Android Auto
articles.summary: Google announced that its Gemini AI assistant is now available for Android Auto for help with navigation, errands, or just brainstorming.
articles.body: Move over Google Assistant, there’s a new robot to yell at while driving. Starting today, Google is rolling out its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto users, allowing drivers access to a “truly conversational” voice assistant who can help with directions, messages, and errands. With Gemini, “you can just speak naturally, have a back and forth conversation and get more complex tasks done,” says Guemmy Kim, Senior Director of Product & User Experience, Android for Cars, in a blog post published today. Customers will need to download the Gemini app on their Android phone, which they will then see on their car’s infotainment display while projecting Android Auto. They can then activate the AI assistant by saying “Hey Google,” pressing the mic button on their car screen, or long pressing the voice control button on their steering wheel. To be sure, Gemini is not available for users Apple CarPlay, nor will it be anytime soon. Google spokesperson Sofia Giovannello said the company didn’t have any updates to share on that front. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: For months, Google has been cramming Gemini to a host of platforms it controls, from Chrome to Google Maps to Nest and Google Home products. But Android Auto is among the first attempts to bring the AI chatbot in to the world of driving. Google says that vehicles with its built-in Android operating systems will be next; Polestar, for example, recently announced that a future software update would bring Gemini to its lineup of electric sports cars. Gemini should offer a step change over the current crop of voice assistants, Google claims. For example, you can ask it for help finding restaurants with a specific cuisine, tell it to message your friends with your ETA with an added emoji, check your calendar for events, make a to-do list, and find addresses buried in your emails. And most importantly, you can purportedly do all this while keeping your hands on the wheel and your eyes on the road. Google says that Gemini can also just hang and chat if that’s what you want. According to Kim, the chatbot can “help you learn something new, brainstorm ideas, rehearse for important moments and much more, all in one continuous conversation.” But will this help drivers focus on the task of driving, or just be another distraction? There’s early research that suggests that speech-based voice assistants in the car are associated with “a rather moderate than high level of cognitive distraction.” There is an assumption that anything that helps prevent you from looking at your phone while driving is an improvement, but that might not necessarily be the case. More research will be needed, especially as tech companies rush to introduce more powerful, AI assistants to the in-car experience.

articles.title: Apple’s chip chief might be the next exec to leave
articles.summary: Apple’s chip chief, Johny Srouji is “seriously considering” leaving for another company in the near future.
articles.body: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is reporting that Johny Srouji, senior vice president of hardware technologies, told Tim Cook he is “seriously considering” leaving Apple for another company in the near future. It was reported in October that Srouji was “evaluating his future at the tech giant.” While nothing is confirmed, it seems the executive is leaning toward not having a future at Cupertino. If Srouji leaves, he would be just the latest in a string of high-profile shakeups in the company’s C-suite. COO Jeff Williams announced his retirement in July, which led to some shifting of roles. But things have only accelerated in December, with AI chief John Giannandrea stepping down, policy lead Lisa Jackson and general counsel Kate Adams announcing plans to retire, and UI design lead Alan Dye departing for Meta, all in the last few days. Apple has struggled somewhat to find its footing as the industry further embraces AI. Now Tim Cook is tasked with trying to stem the bleeding, while being subject to rumors of his own departure. Gurman, who is usually reliable, has said those rumors are premature, but it still adds to the uncertainty surrounding what is typically one of the more stable companies in Silicon Valley.

articles.title: Roborock’s Rover walks, jumps, and vacuums your stairs
articles.summary: Roborock’s latest robot vacuum has articulating legs on wheels, but no price or release date.
articles.body: I’ve been reviewing robot vacuums for almost a decade, and one question I hear repeatedly is “When will it clean my stairs?” Well, we finally have an answer. Sort of. At CES 2026 this week, Roborock launched the Saros Rover, a robot vacuum with articulating legs on wheels that let it climb a full staircase in order to clean multiple floors and also clean each step along the way. I saw a live demo of the Rover on the show floor, and it was impressive. Its legs move in a froglike manner, fluidly and with lots of flexibility. It can raise and lower each one independently, do small jumps, and change direction quickly — moving much more smoothly than most robot vacuums. [Media: As for stairs, it climbed them by using its legs to lift its body, then lowering itself onto the step before pivoting on one leg to vacuum along it. It then proceeded to the next step. The process was fairly slow, taking just under three minutes to climb five stairs, and there were a few moments where it teetered on the edge of a step and I was sure it was going to tumble backwards — but it didn’t. While I’m skeptical that this will entirely eliminate the dust bunnies in the corners of my stairs, it’s a big step up for sure. The Saros also successfully navigated a slope, rolling down it smoothly with control. Roborock said its engine enables it to brake and stop, turn around, and move backward up a slope. In the demo, it also did a small hop, which should let it navigate multi-level room thresholds by jumping over them. [Video: Roborock Rover] I’m told the Rover can climb down stairs using the same method it does going up, and can also go up and down without vacuuming if you want it to move a bit faster, say, to clean your upstairs rooms. Roborock says the Rover will be able to climb almost any staircase, including traditional, curved, spiral, and carpeted staircases with bullnose fronts. Although the stairs I saw it demoed on were wide, flat, and straight. All of this combined should mean the Rover can access every room of your house. There are no specs or a release date for Rover. But the company says it is a real product in development. Roborock is moving cautiously here following the poorly reviewed Saros Z70, its robot vacuum with an arm. “It will take a while to reach the market,” Ruben Rodriguez of Roborock told The Verge. Additionally, the Rover is currently only a vacuum; it doesn’t have a mopping system. “We’re still working out which of our mop systems will work or whether we do a different thing altogether,” said Rodriguez. The evolution of the robot vacuum [Image: Roborock’s Rover and Z70 vacuum with an arm did a little dance on the CES show floor. Yes it was slightly terrifying. We knew this was coming. At CES last year, Roborock and Dreame both debuted vacuums with arms; Dreame’s even had little legs (not staircase-climbing appendages but small propellers that enable it to get over small steps). Then, at IFA 2025, several companies rolled out stair lifts for robot vacuums. The first vacuum robot that can walk up and down your stairs, while also cleaning them, felt inevitable. It’s impressive, but whether it will be practical and affordable remains to be seen. What’s really remarkable is what this signals. Robot vacuums are evolving faster than ever. From simple disc bots that just sucked up dirt to machines that can pick up clutter, clean more than just your floors, and even climb stairs, they’re becoming more capable. Roborock hasn’t given Rover a robotic arm yet, but it’s just a matter of time. All of which indicates that the path to the humanoid home robot may start from the ground up. [Video: Roborock Rover]

articles.title: SC: PRF descobre carga clandestina de emagrecedor em bateria de carro | G1
articles.standfirst: Os envolvidos foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos. O compartimento da bateria do veículo foi adaptado com baterias de moto para esconder os produtos clandestinos.
articles.summary: Os envolvidos foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos. O compartimento da bateria do veículo foi adaptado com baterias de moto para esconder os produtos clandestinos.
articles.body:
Mais de 60 itens - entre ampolas de emagrecedores, frascos de anabolizantes e cigarros eletrônicos - foram flagrados sendo transportados clandestinamente na BR-101 em Joinville , cidade mais populosa de Santa Catarina , no Norte do estado.

Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF),o motorista e o passageiro contaram que alugaram o veículo para fazer uma viagem rápida de ida e volta até Foz do Iguaçu (PR), cidade que faz fronteira com o Paraguai. Os dois foram detidos e os produtos, apreendidos.

Durante a revista pessoal, os agentes encontraram ampolas de emagrecedores escondidas nas roupas dos suspeitos e caixas de medicamentos sob as palmilhas dos calçados.

Ao serem questionados se havia mais irregularidades, um dos ocupantes confessou que existiam outros produtos escondidos sob o capô do carro.

No compartimento da bateria do veículo, adaptado com baterias menores de moto para abrir espaço, os policiais acharam os frascos de anabolizantes. Chaves específicas para retirar a peça estavam guardadas junto ao estepe.

Os dois foram encaminhados à delegacia da Polícia Federal de Joinville.

Segundo a PF, o transporte ou a comercialização de medicamentos clandestinos se enquadra no crime de adulteração de produto destinado a fins terapêuticos ou medicinais. A pena prevista é de 10 a 15 anos de reclusão.

articles.title: Not everyone is loving their new iPhone Duo
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo went on sale just over two weeks ago, but some early adopters have seen enough.
articles.body: For most new relationships, two weeks probably isn’t enough time to decide if you’re ready for long-term commitment. But two weeks with a new phone? You probably know. The iPhone Duo launched just over two weeks ago, and that’s been enough time for a subset of day-one buyers who aren’t loving the phone to make a decision: It’s time to end things. Also, they wanted their $2,000 back. This is to be expected, to an extent; the Duo just isn’t a phone for everyone. It’s an early adopter device — we called it “a messy, expensive good time” — and on top of that, the hinge appears to be suffering some first-gen growing pains. Despite all that, Apple seems to be selling Duos just fine, with new online orders projected to ship in January. As Apple’s customary 14-day return window came to a close, I reached out to a few people to learn more about why they brought their new Duos back. Some of it felt familiar — the outer screen is small, the cameras aren’t great — but other reasons were a little more surprising. Like the fact that the Duo’s whole proposition as a two-in-one device is sometimes a con, not a pro. [Media: “If I can have an iPad in my pocket, that would be great.” So thought Ben Seligson, a content creator, photographer, and now former iPhone Duo owner. After spending some time with the phone, he discovered that having a phone that’s also your iPad wasn’t always ideal. With two separate devices, Seligson told me, “Usually I’d throw a YouTube video on the iPad or throw a podcast up. And then I start cooking dinner and leave my iPad in one spot, but I’d have my phone in my pocket if I got a text, or I needed to set a timer or something like that.” With the Duo, the phone was also the iPad on the counter, so a quick reply became much more of an interruption. Less surprising: A couple of Duo owners I talked to weren’t interested enough in the form factor to try an Android foldable. Not for a lack of curiosity; rather, the iPhone lock-in feels too strong. Michael Hayes, another former Duo owner, says, “I used to flip back and forth between Android and iOS about 10 years ago, and I think I still have a Pixel in a drawer somewhere … Unless something massive changes, I’m locked into the ecosystem now.” Seligson has been tempted by Samsung’s foldables in the past. “A year ago when the Fold 7 came out I was kind of thinking about it,” he says. “But my whole family uses FaceTime; I’m on FaceTime with them all the time. I’ve got the Mac, I’ve got the iPad. So there’s just too many reasons not to try it.” Both Hayes and Seligson switched back to slab-style iPhones rather than other foldables. Fayethe Vongsouvanh, an art director, envisioned using the Duo for editing photos and planning their wedding. They had the misfortune of a cracked screen on the second day of owning the Duo. “At the time, I was at home recovering from hand surgery, so I knew there was no way I was too rough with it,” says Vongsouvanh. They were able to get a replacement quickly, but a number of other quirks led them to return that one, too. Weight was the biggest factor. “The phone is just too heavy and bulky for my daily use,” they say. [Media: Even though things didn’t work out, the Duo seems to have had an impact on the people I spoke to. “There’s a specialness that the Duo has that I kind of miss,” says Seligson. “It felt different, and it didn’t feel like the same phone everyone’s had for the last ten years.” Spending time with the Duo has inspired others to look at old form factors with a fresh perspective. Vongsouvanh enjoyed writing and drawing with the Duo’s inner screen and an Apple Pencil and has been inspired to pick up an older device more often. “I’ll definitely start using my old iPad Pro with a Paperlike screen protector more often,” they say. For Hayes, the Duo led him to downsize. “If there’s one thing the Duo did, it steered me toward the regular Pro instead of the Pro Max this time because it felt comically big after using the Duo.” Maybe small phones have a chance after all. If you’re still waiting for your Duo, there’s some good news; Apple’s holiday return policy kicked in on November 6th, so anyone who’s just getting their phone will have until January 8th, 2027, to return it for a full refund. Even if you don’t end up keeping the phone, you’re probably in for a good time. I’m still using it as my daily driver a few weeks later, and it keeps managing to surprise me with new tricks. But keep an eye on that return window — just in case.

articles.title: New Shaquille O’Neal game show draws ridicule over absurd premise
articles.summary: ‘Can You Hide... Shaq?’ is coming to ABC
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal is set to become the unlikely star of a new hide-and-seek-inspired game show, in which contestants will be tasked with concealing his 7-foot-1-inch frame.

The former NBA star will feature in ABC's Can You Hide... Shaq? , hosted by comedian Nicole Byer.

According to Variety , the show will see eight contestants competing to hide the 7ft 1in sports legend in plain sight around Dallas.

The series logline reads: "In the fast, funny and unpredictable challenges, contestants first split into two teams, each with a set mission and time clock.

"The team that completes its mission with the fewest spottings earns immunity for one team member in the next round, who then becomes team captain.

"The teams must work together toward one greater mission: earning prize money to add to the 'Shaq-pot' that will ultimately be claimed by one winner."

Shaq has promised plenty of fun for viewers.

He said in a statement: "I'm 7-foot-1. I'm not exactly easy to miss.

"I love meeting people wherever I go, but for years I've always wondered, could somebody actually make me disappear? Well, we finally decided to put it to the test.

"We turned it into a real competition, and I can't wait for you to see the creative, ridiculous ways they tried to hide me in plain sight.

"The stakes are high, and so is the prize. But you know me, we're gonna have some fun along the way."

On social media, the concept quickly drew ridicule, with one person comparing it to a sketch from 30 Rock .

They shared a photo of Alec Baldwin's network executive character, Jack Donaghy, speaking to Tina Fey's TV writer character, Liz Lemon, alongside the caption: "The premise is simple, Lemon: Contestants must hide Shaquille O'Neal from the people of Dallas. If this works, the network is ready to greenlight similar shows like 'Will You Co-Sign Lenny Dykstra's Loan?' and 'Can You Convince a Georgia Football Player to Call an Uber?'"

Shaq previously revealed how 12 months of success in 1996 forced him to maintain a level of focus that helped shape the rest of his career.

During that single year, Shaquille joined the Los Angeles Lakers after four seasons with the Orlando Magic, represented the United States at the Atlanta Olympics, was selected for the NBA's 50th Anniversary Team, released his third studio album, You Can't Stop the Reign, and starred as a genie in the fantasy comedy Kazaam.

Shaq told People magazine: "That was probably one of my years where I had to be focused every day."

He added: "I'm a guy that likes to go up and down with my focus on purpose, of course, because I always like to get away from it and then get back. But that year, there was so much coming, so much expectation, so many opportunities."

Can You Hide... Shaq? will premiere with two episodes on Thursday, December 3, at 9 p.m. on ABC and the ESPN app. Episodes will stream on Hulu the next day.

articles.title: Arjun Bijlani opens up about fatherhood, shares the values he wants to instil in son Ayaan; says, "I feel it’s my responsibility to lead by example"
articles.summary: Actor Arjun Bijlani has opened up about fatherhood and the values he hopes to instil in his son, Ayaan.
articles.body: Actor Arjun Bijlani has opened up about fatherhood and the values he hopes to instil in his son, Ayaan. In an exclusive quote shared with IANS, the ‘Naagin’ actor believes that parenting goes beyond teaching children the difference between right and wrong, as it also involves leading by example.Emphasizing the importance of kindness, respect and empathy, Arjun shared that he wants his son to grow up as a confident, independent and compassionate individual who respects everyone.Speaking about the values he wishes to pass on to his son, Arjun believes that parenting is as much about leading by example as it is about teaching. “I think kindness, respect and empathy are extremely important. As a father to Ayaan, I feel it’s my responsibility to lead by example. Children observe everything we do, so they learn more from our actions than our words. I want Ayaan to grow up being confident, independent, respectful towards everyone and, most importantly, a good human being.”Recalling the things he loved doing as a child, the actor admitted that he sometimes misses the carefree days when life was all about playing outdoors and spending time with friends. However, fatherhood has given him an opportunity to revisit those beautiful moments. “I loved playing outdoors with friends, spending hours doing absolutely nothing and not having to worry about time! I do miss those carefree days sometimes. But now, having Ayaan in my life gives me an opportunity to relive some of those childhood moments. Whether it’s playing with him, enjoying his little stories or seeing his excitement about school activities like Children’s Day, I get to experience that magic all over again,” he shared.Talking about his fondest childhood memories ahead of Children’s Day, Arjun shared, “Children’s Day was always exciting because it was one day when school felt more like a celebration than studies! I remember the fun, performances, games and spending time with friends. Now, as a father, I get to experience that excitement all over again through Ayaan. He looks forward to Children’s Day celebrations at school, and seeing his excitement makes me nostalgic about my own childhood. articles.title: I tried Google’s AI glasses and Meta’s finally got real competition
articles.summary: The Android XR experience is better thanks to Gemini, Google’s privacy protections are more proactive, and Warby Parker and Gentle Monster add style.
articles.body: It’s a weird time to launch a new pair of smart glasses. These last few years, Meta has been the dominant player in pushing a fragile smart glasses resurgence. Unfortunately, its privacy reputation led to the “pervert glasses” moniker. Smart glasses have never been more unpopular. But in the past week, I’ve been demoing some new smart glasses from Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster. Some are retro chic frames. Others have the same Y2K vibe as the Matrix films. All were made by Samsung and have Google’s Gemini built in via Android XR, Google’s platform for smart glasses and mixed-reality headsets. The AI demos are better than I expected. In one, I’m sitting in an avant-garde art installation as creepy heads float above my head. On the loudspeaker, words blare in French, Spanish, Korean, and German. Pressing two fingers to my temple, Gemini starts translating each language seamlessly in real time. In another demo, a TV chef cooks a “monster pasta” recipe in Korean while people have a conversation behind me. Music in another language is playing overhead. This exact scenario tripped up the Meta Ray-Ban Display’s translation capabilities when I was on vacation. Here it’s no big deal. I don’t even have to specify the languages I need translated or, as with Meta’s glasses, download a specific language pair to translate. I sit at another table with an English speaker, a Thai speaker, and the glasses translate everything they say to me — correctly — into Japanese. [Image: Gentle Monster’s styles have a bolder, Y2K vibe. But I was most surprised that the glasses automatically redact faces from any photo or video to protect bystander privacy. I asked Gemini to identify my video director, Owen Grove. Gemini told me it knew I was looking at a person, but it can’t identify him because of privacy protections. We pull up a picture of our editor-in-chief, Nilay Patel. There, too, Gemini said that for privacy reasons, it can’t identify a person from a photo either. Meta’s glasses also can’t do this. But what’s striking here is that Google is making an active choice to take facial recognition completely off the table. The Warby Parker and Gentle Monster glasses have the customary privacy LED light that lights up whenever there’s an intent to save visual data. Like Meta’s glasses, there’ll be protections in place to disable the glasses if tampering is detected. However, when I sit down to chat with Juston Payne, Google’s senior director of product management for XR, he says Google intends to go much further than the LED light. “Somebody might come up with some solution [to tamper with privacy LEDs] that our algorithms can’t detect, so then the question becomes: So what can we do?” says Payne. “We’re not going to target ads on it. We’re not going to train Gemini on it. Humans aren’t going to be able to use it to improve the models. We’re also redacting faces before they actually go to the server in the first place, which then gets ahead of certain things that can obviously go sideways if you don’t take those steps proactively.” It’s not just faces that’ll get redacted either. Payne tells me that ambient noise — like bystander conversations — will also get scrubbed. The glasses will only process audio from the glasses-wearer using beam-forming mics. Camera and mic access will also require opt-in permissions. [Image: This photo was taken on a Gentle Monster pair. The camera is 12MP. Alone, these are a bold departure from Meta’s approach to smart glasses. Locally redacting faces and ambient audio, for example, is a conscious choice to give up a valuable source of training data. Google could leave it at that, and Android XR would already have a leg up in the privacy discussion. But Payne says Google plans on using its entire platform to disincentivize glassholes. For example, YouTube will crack down on any creepy videos featuring harassment or unwanted sexualization, regardless of how they’re captured. Google Shopping and Google Ads won’t allow sales or ads for accessories like lens covers for privacy LED lights. Google Play policies will prohibit third-party apps from enabling social livestreaming, real-time facial identification, or changing anything about how the LED light functions. Payne also says third-party apps requiring camera or mic API access will need further review to prove they’re being used responsibly. This is less of a concern right now, but it’s a future-focused stance for other Android XR devices or even with devices like Xreal’s Aura glasses. It’s hard to gauge how effective this privacy policy will be with the public. We’ll have to see how it’s received. It’s much more expansive than Meta’s more reactive approach so far. Granted, Meta doesn’t have its own app store or a computing platform quite like Android. This still underscores how much more Meta could’ve been doing all along. The one area Meta truly nailed with smart glasses has been style. The company, through its partnership with EssilorLuxottica, has over 100 combinations of frames and lenses. Samsung’s partnerships with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster aren’t too shabby to look at. Warby Parker has three designs and three colors: green, brown, and black. Gentle Monster has six frames — including two that are very Y2K — with bolder designs, colors, and tinted lens options. The Warby Parker collection starts at $395, while Gentle Monster starts at $449. Style-wise, I found both collections were fetching. Warby Parker was a bit more everyday, whereas Gentle Monster felt a bit more editorial and runway-ready. Most people should be able to find a look that fits their needs. The glasses are fairly lightweight (for smart glasses) at 41g. Battery life is estimated at around nine hours, while the cases support up to seven extra charges. Sound quality is pretty good, and the 12MP ultrawide camera takes decent photos and video with image stabilization. So, head tilters rejoice! Your accidental Dutch-angle photos will be straightened. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Media: Where Android XR excels is that Gemini on the glasses is, so far, more capable than Meta AI on the Ray-Bans. I was able to look at an event flyer for a concert in Mumbai, have Gemini add the details to Google Calendar, and then look up flight details to India. It gave me turn-by-turn walking directions while also telling me the event schedule for the Whitney Museum. Beginning a live translation doesn’t require me to download a specific language pair onto my phone like with the Ray-Bans. I was also surprised to see Gemini occasionally correct itself in real-time when it made a mistake, or ask me to get a different view of an object I was trying to identify so it could deliver a more accurate answer. Low-vision and blind users aren’t left out either. The glasses feature Google’s Guided Vision, which offers conversational audio descriptions of environments and surroundings. Android XR is also collaborating with Aira, which allows users to stream what they’re seeing using the camera to a real-time human interpreter. At launch, this particular feature will be for Android users only, but otherwise the glasses will work regardless of your phone. [Image: Warby Parker’s collection is more everyday chic. Leaving my hands-on, it’s never been clearer that technology isn’t currently the issue with smart glasses. Whether or not this form factor takes off will boil down to culture, privacy, and usefulness. And on that front, this space has been stagnating a bit because Meta has been the sole big player setting the tone and pushing the conversation. The Android XR approach is notably different, and serious competition for Meta is excellent for consumers. All that’s left is to see whose approach wins. You can preorder Gentle Monster and Warby Parker smart glasses starting today, and the devices are expected to ship starting December 10th.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns, chipmaker names CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia gets a new chief executive, days after former CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company said on Thursday, just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis.

In a regulatory filing , Nvidia said its board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday.

Nvidia said its current chief financial officer and executive vice president, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO until the company finds a permanent successor. Kress will continue to serve as the company’s CFO.

Nvidia’s shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company’s stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion.

Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it as CEO ever since. Under his leadership, Nvidia played a crucial role in developing the graphics processing unit (GPU), a specialized chip that does graphics processing for PCs, as we know it today. The chips were not an immediate hit, and the early days of Nvidia were characterized by struggle and layoffs, but eventually, it struck on a GPU design that performed so well, it became the standard for graphics processing.

These chips also turned out to be extremely good at doing large numbers of calculations simultaneously, which has made them popular for computation-intensive tasks like crypto mining, and more recently, training and running neural networks, which are what AI models are at their core.

Nvidia was initially focused on making GPUs aimed at gaming, but it had already moved into general-purpose computing by 2006 with the launch of the CUDA architecture, which lets developers use the chips for other tasks, such as doing calculations and research. After AI researchers began using the company’s GPUs to train neural networks over a decade ago, Huang leaned in toward developing chips for AI and then data centers, and grew it from there into its dominant position.

Under Huang, the company has been by far the biggest beneficiary of the AI industry’s skyrocketing growth, which has largely depended on Nvidia’s GPUs for training and running large language models. Before ChatGPT launched and sparked the AI boom, Nvidia shares were trading at about $15. As of last month, they had risen more than 1,450% to an all-time high of $243. Its market cap consequently has also risen by an eye-watering $5.5 trillion since then, reaching as high as $5.88 trillion early in October.

Revenue, of course, has also ballooned, rising more than 1,500% to $96.22 billion as of the company’s second quarter, from $5.93 billion in Q3 2023, right before the ChatGPT moment. Profits increased nearly 88 times in that period to $59.69 billion as of July 2026, from $680 million in October 2023.

That success was predicated on large part by the AI industry’s continued development, which Huang seemingly made his personal mission. He traveled to conferences and events around the world to promote his products and AI, lobbied extensively for looser regulation after the Biden administration placed export controls on the sale of high-power AI chips to China, and cultivated a close relationship with Trump, often to Nvidia’s benefit .

The resignation and controversy come at a crucial moment for Nvidia. China was always a big market for the company, though its impact on the company’s finances has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. Chinese customers accounted for revenue of about $7.9 billion in the company’s second quarter, roughly 8% of total revenue.

The potential implications of Huang’s departure for the AI and data center industries are vast, given how active Huang, and by extension Nvidia, has been in furthering the AI boom. In particular, it raises questions about the future of Nvidia’s sprawling AI investments, which have helped bankroll everything from startups developing new technologies to the enormous data centers needed to run them.

Under Huang, Nvidia deftly used its financial muscle to support companies buying its chips, effectively helping to finance the market for its own products, as well as lobbying Washington to relax potential rules around AI and data center regulation.

As of the end of its second quarter, Nvidia reported $99 billion worth of investments and another $25 billion of commitments. It also has $36 billion in cloud service commitments, which are arrangements that help AI cloud operators finance the GPUs and data center equipment they buy from Nvidia, with the chipmaker saying it will buy compute from them and potentially earn a share of their operators’ revenue.

Nvidia has also been investing directly in neoclouds, the companies serving a lot of the AI processing needs. In January, the company invested $2 billion in CoreWeave , and another $2 billion in Nebius in March. The chipmaker was said to be considering being a guarantor for Nscale’s planned West Virginia data center project. It’s also signed up to provide up to $105 billion worth of credit guarantees for an OpenAI data center campus in Ohio.

Nvidia’s also a major investor in the labs building the AI models that run on its GPUs, putting $30 billion into OpenAI, and $10 billion into Anthropic . It’s also backed Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab as part of a deal involving at least 1 GW of its Vera Rubin GPU systems. The chipmaker has also invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek to help the Taiwanese company develop custom AI chips that work with Nvidia’s systems.

Many investors have grown uneasy with the enormous amounts of debt companies in the space were raising to sustain the AI infrastructure buildout, and Huang’s exit throws another uncertainty-shaped wrench into the works. CoreWeave’s shares were down about 9% on Thursday, reversing part of a 25% rally on Wednesday, while Nebius is down about 16%. IREN fell 6.6%.

Nvidia’s board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. As chair, Jones is likely to play a central role in Nvidia’s search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang.

Huang is the single largest personal shareholder at Nvidia, but he owns only about 3.5% of the company’s shares. Unlike many of Silicon Valley’s tech giants, he does not hold supervoting rights, and the board had the power to vote him out at any time.

Huang famously ran a very flat organization, with around 60 direct reports. There was no heir apparent or succession plan either (although two of his children also worked in executive roles at the company). Huang famously maintained tight control over the company he founded, making it challenging for Nvidia to find a path forward without him.

The industry will get its first glimpse of that next week during the quarterly conference call. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the company said in a statement.

Note: This story was updated to add details about Nvidia’s growth and Huang’s efforts to promote AI development, as well as its focus on China.

articles.body: Bricklink, a popular online marketplace that Lego bought in 2019 where fans can buy and sell parts and sets, has been down for a week and the company doesn’t know when it will return. The team who runs the site has been sharing updates over the past week including estimates of when it will be back up. It was last expected to return on November 11th, according to Jay’s Brick Blog, but a statement Lego shared to the site yesterday says there’s currently no estimate of when BrickLink will be back online. Lego hasn’t explained exactly what happened with the marketplace, but says it “took BrickLink offline after identifying unusual activity on the platform. Our immediate priority was to secure the site, protect our members and ensure the integrity of BrickLink.” There are also no specifics on when BrickLink will return, as Lego works to contain what happened. “Before bringing the site back online, we need to fully understand what has happened. That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues.” Three years ago, BrickLink experienced a similar issue around the same time of year resulting in the marketplace being offline for several days due to a cybersecurity incident. Lego shut down the site “out of an abundance of caution” after receiving a “threat and ransom demand.” When BrickLink returned, users were prompted to change their passwords with stronger requirements, but were assured their accounts had not been compromised during the incident.

articles.title: Google Wallet can finally unlock doors with digital home keys
articles.summary: Google has added digital home key support to Google Wallet, allowing Android users to open smart locks by tapping their phone against them or simply approaching.
articles.body: Google has added digital home key support to Google Wallet, allowing Android users to open smart locks by tapping their phone against them or simply approaching. The feature is currently available in public preview for the Google Home app, and will roll out to everyone “over the coming weeks,” according to Google’s announcement. This was a long time coming, given Samsung and Apple users have had this convenience for a while now. While Google Home already has some unlocking functionality, this update allows users to leverage the Near Field Communication (NFC) and Ultra-Wideband (UWB) tech in their phones with compatible smart locks. Multiple locks can be controlled via Google Wallet using a single digital home key. All household members linked to the same Google Home account can also add their own key to their personal Google Wallet. Tap to Unlock works by holding the back of an NFC-enabled Android phone near the lock reader, and doesn’t require the phone to be unlocked. Unlock on Approach needs to be manually enabled in Google Wallet, but can automatically unlock a door when it detects the user walking up. [Image: This is what Google Wallet users will see when they setup a digital home key. There are a few compatibility requirements to bear in mind, however. These new Google Home capabilities are built on Aliro, the open standard designed to let any smartphone unlock any smart lock, but the hardware that supports it is still fairly limited. According to Google’s announcement, the list of supported locks currently includes the Aqara u400, Schlage Sense Pro (NFC at launch and UWB to follow), and Nuki Keypad 2 NFC, with “more locks to come.” Users will also need a Matter-enabled Google Hub with Thread Border Router, such as the 2nd-gen Nest Hub. Tap to unlock requires NFC-enabled phones running Android 9 or later, and hands-free unlocking only works on Aliro UWB-compatible Android phones, such as the Google Pixel 10 Pro series and above. Wear OS smartwatches aren’t supported “at launch,” according to Google, which implies they might be in the future, and that seems likely given that Apple Watch already has similar unlocking features.

articles.title: ‘The end of Tesla!’: Cybertruck diehards turn on Elon Musk after he pulls the plug
articles.summary: Elon Musk is ending Cybertruck production to prioritize the Cybercab, sparking rare backlash from diehard Tesla influencers and loyal fans on X and YouTube.
articles.body: The Cybertruck is heading to that shiny cyber-dumpster in the sky, leaving the folks who built online identities around Elon Musk’s polarizing pickup feeling bereft. Usually, Musk’s fanbase treads lightly around their idol’s mercurial decisions. This time, however, the truck’s demise has sparked rare backlash within the Tesla community — aimed squarely at the guy who signed its death warrant. Troy Meekhof, who posts on numerous social platforms under the moniker “The Cybertruck Guy,” has been vocal about his disappointment in Musk’s decision to wind down Cybertruck production by the end of summer 2027. (The original plan was to start winding down production in the spring, but then Musk decided to extend it a few months.) In a 33-minute video on YouTube, Meekhof argues that Tesla never fully committed to making the Cybertruck a success, citing a lack of advertising, confusing pricing changes, and the decision to shift focus before the truck could fully establish itself in the market. “It feels like they didn’t try to make Cybertruck a success,” he said. [Media: He also had choice words for Musk’s reasons for ending the Cybertruck’s short run to make room at Giga Texas for the fully autonomous Cybercab: “Cancelling all of your best products... in favor of an autonomous platform that remains both software and regulatory constrained... seems like an absolutely terrible idea,” Meekhof vented. The Cybertruck wasn’t the only Tesla product to meet an untimely end — at least according to those with stakes (and often stock options) in the company’s success. Earlier this year, Tesla discontinued the Model S and Model X, two of its flagship vehicles. With the end of the Cybertruck, Tesla is now left with just the Model 3 and Model Y as vehicles you can actually buy. (The Semi is strictly a commercial vehicle, while the Cybercab’s availability as a consumer product remains dubious, at best.) “Cancelling Cybertruck after all the years of getting it to production to ‘make room for CyberCab’ is a lame excuse,” @TeslaXplored wrote on X. “There are like 500 CyberCabs in one city that only Tesla influencers are riding in. Taking away consumer cars instead of building what the people want will be the end of Tesla!” He added, “Very sad what happened to Tesla over the last 5 years.” [Media: Meanwhile, at least one prominent aftermarket company is offering to step in and pick up the mantle. Unplugged Performance, which makes aftermarket accessories, said it would produce the Cybertruck and other vehicles on the truck platform under license, with investors funding the effort: “Worth a conversation?” Musk, for his part, seems less interested in litigating the particulars of Cybertruck production and more intent on selling a vision of Tesla’s future centered around the Cybercab and humanoid robots. “Cybercab will do a majority of all passenger miles in any jurisdiction where it is not prohibited by law,” Musk wrote on X earlier this week. “Obvious to anyone with eyes and a brain.” He also pushed back on claims that the Cybertruck was killed because it was unprofitable. “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate,” Musk said. “We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.” To be sure, Cybertruck sales have been disappointing over its entire production run. Musk initially theorized that Tesla could sell 250,000-500,000 Cybertrucks annually, but the actual numbers have been far below those projections. Last year, Tesla is estimated to have sold around 20,000 trucks; the company is on track to sell fewer than that this year. Whether Musk’s autonomous utopia pans out or ends up joining the Cybertruck in the vaporware graveyard remains to be seen. For now, the stainless-steel wedge that was supposed to be the ultimate symbol of an indestructible future has become a monument to Musk’s shifting attention span — and a stark reminder to Tesla’s most loyal boosters that in Elon’s world, nothing should be taken for granted.

articles.title: GOP lawmaker says party is focusing on ‘political power’ rather than people
articles.summary: Texas Rep. Chip Roy (R) issued a scathing rebuke of the Republican Party on Thursday, after the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections last week. Roy, who will depart his role on Jan. 3 after launching an unsuccessful bid for Texas attorney general, spoke for nearly half an hour…
articles.body:
Texas Rep. Chip Roy (R) issued a scathing rebuke of the Republican Party on Thursday, after the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections last week.

Roy, who will depart his role on Jan. 3 after launching an unsuccessful bid for Texas attorney general, spoke for nearly half an hour on the House floor.

In what could mark his final speech before the body, the Texas Republican accused his party of “trying to focus on political power” instead of acting in the best interests of their constituents.

“It pisses me off,” he said. “The arrogance of the powers that be, the masters of the universe who tell you that that’s what you have to do. And when you pursue political power over the people, you lose, and that’s what happened.”

Following the GOP’s losses last week, Roy has publicly aired his grievances with the direction his party took in these elections.

Specifically, the Republican reupped his criticism of his party’s decision to back Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton (R) against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) in the state’s GOP primary.

Paxton, who was ultimately defeated in the general election by Texas state Rep. James Talarico (D), faced a series of controversies related to his past conduct. He was impeached by the Texas House of Representatives for alleged inappropriate favors done for donors, then later acquitted by the state Senate.

“Somebody tell me why Republicans lost last Tuesday, I’ll say it’s because they were focused on themselves and the ruling class and not the people,” Cornyn said, after referencing Paxton’s campaign. “The founders gave us a system that does put the people first, and when politicians forget that, they rightly get sent home.”

The Texas Republican also cautioned Democrats who are celebrating their wins in last week’s elections.

“The people right now are not in love with either party,” he said. “Democrats who right now think they’re all fired up that they’re on some sort of wave, no sir.”

“Republicans who think they’ve got all the answers, ‘Oh, if we’d have just not done Iran, man, we were just sailing along.’ No,” Roy continued. “It’s the people who are tired of seeing corporate crony government interests steamroll their way of life, steamroll their community.”

Roy, who has urged Congress to stay in session until Jan. 3, called on his party to push forward its legislative priorities in their remaining time in power, including a congressional stock trading ban, border security and a reconciliation package.

“These are the things that people sent us here to do and more, again all designed to try to preserve and protect our great country, to actually secure it,” Roy said.

articles.title: Whoop launched a social network where every user has a ‘verified heartbeat’
articles.summary: Whoop launched a new social network in its app called Whoop Humans, where users can share data from their wearable.
articles.body: Starting Thursday, Whoop members can share their data from its wearables on the app’s new Whoop Humans social network. Users can make their metrics, activities, and achievements visible to other Whoop wearers, post Story-like “Moments” with photos and captions, and add comments and reactions on other members’ posts. Whoop claims its platform is “entirely human,” unlike other social media platforms that are “saturated with artificial intelligence, automated accounts and bots, and manufactured content.” Whoop CEO Will Ahmed says Humans is “the most verifiably human network ever launched. Every account represents a real person with a verified heartbeat.” Whoop says its existing Teams social feature “will remain available,” allowing people to share strain, recovery, and sleep data along with group leaderboards. In the Community tab in Whoop’s app, users can scroll through Moments from people they’re following, like tapping through your Stories feed on Instagram but with your friends’ fitness tracker data. In one of Whoop’s examples, swiping up on a user’s Moments post with a photo from their run shows a map with their route and details like their pace and distance. The Community tab also shows cards for people in your “community” with their sleep, recovery, and strain scores. Whoop says users choose which activities, achievements, and metrics they want to share on Humans, including Recovery, Strain, Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate. Any activities marked as sensitive aren’t shared by default. There’s also an option to keep Moments posts private and a “Stealth Mode” for temporarily hiding health and performance data without changing your sharing settings.

articles.title: Donald Trump really wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia
articles.summary: President Donald Trump is already throwing around one person he thinks should take over Nvidia: former Apple CEO Tim Cook.
articles.body: Jensen Huang resigned this morning as Nvidia’s CEO following reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Right now, the company is being led by its CFO on an interim basis. But President Donald Trump is already throwing around one person he thinks should take over the chipmaking giant: former Apple CEO Tim Cook, who stepped down from leading the company on September 1st and moved into an executive chairman role. Shortly after Huang’s resignation was announced today, Trump posted his idea about Cook on Truth Social: “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” In a new episode of Stephen A. Smith’s Straight Shooter podcast published today, Trump made his pitch for Cook again, saying that Apple “would never be what it is today” if Steve Jobs was still “around”: > Can [Huang] be replaced? > Well, you know, the expression, Anybody can be replaced? So it’s very hard to replace him, but I had an idea this morning that I sort of just released: Tim Cook. He just sort of semi-retired from Apple. He’s done one of the greatest jobs in the history of business. > I think if Tim Cook, who built Apple… If Steve Jobs were around, Apple would never be what it is today. Tim Cook took a lot of these brilliant ideas and designs and everything else from Jobs and others, and he made it into one of the great companies of the world in a fairly short period. I think Tim Cook would be a great candidate to run Nvidia. Apple and Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. Cook is well-known for his ongoing relationship with President Trump, including gifting the president a 24k gold and glass statue last year. (Trump, after Cook announced his transition plan earlier this year, posted a story about having “the head of Apple calling to ‘kiss my ass.’”) During the podcast, Trump said he spoke to Huang yesterday and that Huang is “going through hell”: > Should [Huang] have stepped down? > Well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy, and I don’t know if that’s been determined yet, but if the woman was a spy, yes, if the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different. > But I can tell you this. Somehow, he’ll end up on his feet. I mean, I know him, I know him pretty well. I always thought of him as a fine man. > I spoke to him yesterday. He’s going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family. That’s what he is, really… that’s what he told me. I’m president, and he called me. And he said, What I’ve done to my wife and family is... That’s what he talked about. Trump, on the podcast, called Huang a “tremendous talent.” Other tech leaders have also publicly supported Huang following his resignation.

articles.title: ‘I don’t care’: How Jensen Huang’s last hours as Nvidia CEO unfolded
articles.summary: Jensen Huang's final hours as Nvidia chief executive were marked by exhaustion, resignation and an apparent surrender after weeks of fighting to hold on
articles.body: Jensen Huang's final hours as Nvidia chief executive were marked by exhaustion, resignation and an apparent surrender after weeks of fighting to hold on to his position amid allegations of extramarital affairs and links to a suspected Chinese spy, Bloomberg reported.According to Bloomberg, citing a person familiar with the situation, Huang's usual take-charge demeanour had disappeared. Instead, he had started using phrases such as "whatever" and "I don't careThe Nvidia co-founder, once known for his relentless energy and extraordinary attention to detail, appeared broken by the mounting controversy. Less than a week after admiting infidelity and being embroiled in an alleged espionage plot by a Chinese spy, Huang's resistance had seemingly collapsed by late Wednesday night.The developments came despite an intervention by US President Donald Trump, who called Huang on Tuesday and urged him to fight for his position, The New York Times reported, citing two people briefed on the conversation. Huang, however, resigned on Thursday.The crisis had intensified following reports of Huang's alleged relationships with multiple women, including Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of having links to Beijing's intelligence services. The New York Times also reported that Huang had a second alleged affair with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. Further reports identified the executive as company vice-president Kimberly Powell.The controversy has also raised questions about Nvidia's business and its standing amid growing scrutiny of the artificial intelligence sector. The company's shares fell 4.3% on Thursday after an opening drop of around 14%, recovering some ground during the session. The stock has lost 30.5% since reaching a record high on October 6.Nvidia's troubles have also added to pressure on the broader technology market, given its significant contribution to gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite.Meanwhile, the controversy has spilled into Washington, with the White House reportedly weighing whether to remove Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his handling of technology exports to China. articles.summary: Service is starting to recover for Microsoft Outlook and 365 systems as its outage enters a second day, impacting millions of users around the world.
articles.body: Service is gradually starting to recover for Microsoft Outlook and 365 after an almost two-day outage impacting millions of users around the world. While some apps and features are still running in a degraded state, some people (including Verge staffers) are reporting that access to their emails has been restored, though the flow of Outlook mail might be delayed while efforts to fully fix the outage continue. Charles Lamanna, Copilot, agents, and platform leader at Microsoft said in a statement to The Verge that the situation is continuing to improve: > “We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure. We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward.” Senior Verge correspondent Tom Warren reports that according to his sources, the outage is linked to Azure VNet config changes. Microsoft has said that it hasn’t found any evidence of the outage being connected to “malicious activity,” and that a full report will be shared after the issues are mitigated. In a statement reported by Sky News tech correspondent Rowland Manthorpe, Microsoft described the outage as a “technical issue,” and says it isn’t related to “cyber, AI/agents, DDOS, etc.” [Media: The scope of the outage also affects features in other Microsoft services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and 365 apps. articles.title: Apple should have made the MacBook logo RGB
articles.summary: Apple’s MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display brings back the illuminated lid logo. But since it’s now lit with LEDs, it could have had a pop of color.
articles.body: When Apple CEO John Ternus announced the first touchscreen Mac last month, the biggest reaction in the room wasn’t for the PROLED MacBook Pro’s OLED touchscreen or the thinner and lighter chassis; it was for the illuminated lid logo. It’s a throwback to the light-up logos on the old MacBooks, which Apple started phasing out in 2015, and which were completely gone by the 2018 MacBook Air redesign. It’s a nostalgia play, but boy did it work. It’s fun! Just like in the old days, the new logo’s brightness is linked to the screen’s: The brighter or dimmer the screen, the brighter or dimmer the logo. But the light-up logo on the old MacBooks was illuminated by the screen’s backlight, and an OLED display doesn’t have one. Thanks to iFixit, we now know it’s lit by four white LEDs and synced with the screen’s brightness by software. But that means Apple could have used RGB LEDs. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet, or anything in between? On the lid of your new MacBook Pro? Why not? After all, Apple insists it’s still serious about gaming, and nothing says “serious about gaming” like RGB lighting. [Image: The new LED-illuminated lid logo of the PROLED MacBook Pro (left) next to the opaque black logo of other MacBooks (right). I was secretly hoping users would be able to customize the illuminated lid cutout much like the Xbox logo on Microsoft’s Elite Series 2 controllers. But alas, no luck. You can turn off the illumination with some Terminal commands or take control of it with a third-party app. But when it’s lit, it’s only lit with white light. And iFixit’s teardown also showed the difficulty of accessing those LEDs (the screen delaminated and broke in the process). So we’re unlikely to see LED RGB mods for it unless someone’s brave enough to void their warranty and risk a pricey screen repair on their $3,000 laptop. The most fun you can have with the Apple lid logo is to install a free third-party app like LogoLight and have it pulse, breathe, match the beat of any music you’re playing, or flash some Morse code. There’s some fun there, but if you combined these features with a splash of color we’d really be cooking. [Image: Apps like LogoLight allow you to customize the lid logo, but not with color. MacBooks aren’t gaming laptops, so RGB lighting may seem like a mismatch, but multicolor LEDs could have been a cool Easter egg. Nobody thought Apple would put a touchscreen on a MacBook either, and the iPhone Duo and HomeView also show Apple is in a new age of experimentation during the early Ternus era. Maybe if the light-up lid logo ever comes to future MacBook Airs or a MacBook Neo, Apple could cut loose a little.

articles.title: Apple announces release dates for the first Apple Home Collection smart devices
articles.summary: Several of the Apple Home Collection smart devices are now available for preorder including LG’s cameras and video doorbell.
articles.body: The first few smart home devices and accessories that Apple co-developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric for its new Apple Home Collection are now available for preorder through the company’s online store, with delivery expected in mid-December. Apple announced the collection a month ago as part of a stronger push into the smart home space that’s led by its new Siri AI-powered HomeView smart display which is also now available starting today. Of all the Apple Home Collection devices currently listed on its online store, only a handful of LG accessories are available for preorder. These include the $299.95 LG Outdoor Cam and $199.95 Indoor Cam, plus the $249.95 LG Video Doorbell, which all show an estimated shipping timeline of December 11th to December 17th. The rest of the collection, including the $399.95 LG Floodlight Cam, $349.95 LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, $199.95 LG Smart Thermostat, $199.95 Schneider Home Smart Thermostat, and $39.95 Schneider Home Room Sensor, aren’t yet available for preorder and don’t have an estimated ship date. The devices in the Apple Home Collection don’t include exclusive features or functionality, but through the partnership, Apple has streamlined the setup process so it’s as easy as tapping them with your iPhone to get them running. The devices in the collection also use Thread to remain connected should they lose access to the internet or your Wi-Fi network, and they can automatically update their network credentials if you make changes to your wireless network.
