articles.title: The smallest version of Camp Snap’s retro digital camcorder fits on your keychain
articles.summary: Camp Snap miniaturized its retro digital camcorder once again with the CS-8 Micro that captures 720p video with several vintage filters.
articles.body: Last week, Camp Snap launched a miniaturized version of its screen-free CS-8 video camera that was half the size of the original with a smaller grip designed to be easier for kids to hold. But it turns out the company wasn’t done shrinking its hardware. Camp Snap’s new CS-8 Micro is even smaller than the CS-8 Mini. It’s around three inches long and weighs just 1.5 ounces so you can hang it from your keys and, like its larger predecessors, it can capture video using one of five built-in filters. The CS-8 Micro is now available through Camp Snap’s online store and Urban Outfitters for $39.99, and similar to the collectible Kodak Charmera, the Micro is being sold in sealed mystery boxes. Colors like hot pink, lilac, lime, and orange will be easier to find, while vintage classic (black) and glow in the dark will be much rarer. Unlike the original CS-8 and CS-8 Mini, the new Micro does include an LCD display, but it’s only used as a viewfinder. You can’t watch, edit, or delete anything you’ve captured on the camera itself. You need to transfer the videos to a phone or computer using a USB-C cable to enjoy them, or move its included 4GB microSD into a card reader. [Product: Camp Snap CS-8 Micro | As Camp Snap has been progressively shrinking its retro camcorder, it’s also reduced its resolution. The original captured videos at 4K, while the CS-8 Mini did 2.7K. The CS-8 Micro is limited to 720p, but carries forward features like an 8x digital zoom and a selection of five filters that include vintage effects that add flicker and grain to emulate the look of 8mm film. Camp Snap estimates the Micro’s 4GB microSD card can hold 45 to 6o minutes of video, while its battery life is estimated to be 30 to 45 minutes on a full charge.

articles.title: You can adjust the position of the trackball on Keychron’s new wireless mouse
articles.summary: The T1 HE is Keychron’s next trackball mouse and features an adjustable design so you can improve its ergonomics by repositioning the ball.
articles.body: The Nape Pro was Keychron’s first trackball device that was introduced at CES 2026 with a slim and compact design allowing it to be positioned right up against a keyboard. The company’s new T1 HE instead looks more like other trackball mice already available from companies like Logitech and Kensington with a 34mm ball positioned on the side to improve ergonomics. But since hands and fingers come in various sizes, the T1 HE allows the position of its trackball to be fine-tuned with minor positional adjustments so it rests squarely under your thumb without any reaching. The T1 HE is now available for preorder through Keychron’s online store for $59.99 in black, white, or translucent color options. Shipping is expected to start in early December. A pair of dials on the underside of the mouse are used to adjust the vertical and horizontal position of the trackball, which can also be extended or retracted. The adjustments are limited to just a few millimeters in either direction, but those minor improvements to ergonomics could go a long way to making the T1 HE more comfortable to use on a regular basis. [Image: The T1 HE doesn’t offer extensive trackball adjustments, but even small improvements can result in a more ergonomic and comfortable experience. The sensitivity of the T1 HE’s optical sensor can be adjusted from 100 DPI to 2,400 DPI using a button that cycles through presets or the Keychron Launcher software that also allows for other customizations including button remapping and creating macros. The mouse features six customizable buttons in total, and a 600mAh battery good for up to 106 hours of use in Bluetooth mode, or 98 hours when using an included 2.4GHz wireless receiver. If you don’t want to worry about charging, the T1 HE Wireless Adjustable Trackball Mouse can also be used with a USB-C cable.

articles.title: FAA ground stop shuts down flights nationwide
articles.summary: A “telecommunications outage” has caused the FAA to issue a ground stop order for all domestic flights in the US on Friday.
articles.body: Takeoffs from airports throughout the US largely stopped on Friday after the FAA issued a national ground stop “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” while planes in the air will be allowed to land. The FAA tweeted just after 5PM ET that, “There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis.” The flight tracking site FlightAware lists 10,494 US flights as delayed as of 6:16PM ET. According to CNN, the last nationwide ground stop in 2023 lasted for about 90 minutes after the NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) system for pilots went down, and the last one prior to that was after the attacks on September 11th, 2001. Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday afternoon, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that there is currently no reason to suspect a cyberattack or other national security threat, or any connection to the recent Microsoft Outlook outage, but that so far no cause has been ruled out for the “telecommunications outage.” [Media: When asked about any possible connection to the cloud-based AI Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) system that was activated nationwide on November 10th, he said they were looking into that. Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company that designed the system and was awarded a 12-year $875 million contract in June to deploy it, denied any connection, tweeting “The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC.” Mullin also said international flights and departures are being handled on a case-by-case basis, while NBC News and the New York Times report that some flights headed to Europe and Asia have taken off from Boston and New York. Jon Ostrower of The Air Current reports that the outage began with the Chicago air traffic control center, followed by centers in Boston, Washington, New York, and Minneapolis, and as the FAA issued a ground stop for aircraft flying east, more facilities began reporting problems. He says the problems are disrupting both the radar and radio frequencies used by air traffic controllers and pilots, while a CNN update on Friday cited an unnamed source claiming the FAA “doesn’t know yet what is going on,” with no clear answers about the cause. articles.title: Amazon’s new Kindle Colorsoft is a premium e-reader with a premium price | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The latest model is lighter and thinner than its predecessor and features an edge-to-edge display. But if you already own the first-generation Colorsoft, there’s little reason to upgrade.
articles.body:
Amazon recently unveiled its refreshed Kindle lineup introducing a new basic Kindle , Paperwhite, and Colorsoft. The new Kindle Colorsoft starts at $290, while the Signature Edition, which I’ve spent the past few weeks testing, costs $320.

The base model comes with 16GB of storage, while the Signature Edition doubles that to 32GB and is available in graphite or a maroon-like Fig finish with an aluminum back.

Amazon first brought color to its Kindle lineup in 2024 with the launch of the original Colorsoft. The latest model is lighter and thinner than its predecessor and features an edge-to-edge display. If you already own the first-generation Colorsoft, there’s little reason to upgrade.

The core reading experience remains largely the same. Both models have a 7-inch color E-Ink display, 300ppi resolution for black-and-white content and 150ppi for color.

However, if you’ve been eyeing a color e-reader, the new Colorsoft is worth considering if you can get past the hefty price tag.

Unlike standard Kindles, which display everything in black and white, the Colorsoft brings your digital bookshelf to life with their original colors. This makes it a particularly appealing option for readers who enjoy comics, graphic novels, or cookbooks, where color makes a big difference. It’s also great for readers who like highlighting passages in different colors.

It’s worth noting that colors on the Colorsoft are still relatively muted and not as vibrant as what you’d see on an iPad. Still, they add a welcome splash of color and make a noticeable difference compared to the black-and-white displays of standard Kindles.

The Colorsoft lets you adjust the screen’s color temperature, so you can switch to a warmer, more yellow-toned display that’s easier on the eyes when reading at night. There’s also an auto-adjusting brightness option that comes in handy.

When it comes to battery life, Amazon says that the Colorsoft can last up to eight weeks on a single charge, compared to up to 12 weeks for the Paperwhite. During my testing, I didn’t have to stress about charging the Colorsoft because like other Kindles, its battery lasts a relatively long time compared to other everyday electronics.

One small but welcome improvement on the new Colorsoft is the repositioned power button. On the previous generation, it was on the bottom of the device next to the charging port, making it easy to accidentally press it when handling the Kindle. On the new model, Amazon has moved it to the top-right edge, where it’s less likely to get in the way. I quite like this change, and found the new location more intuitive when powering the device on and off.

I enjoyed the premium feel of the aluminum back on the Signature Edition. Although Amazon provided a case with my review unit, I rarely used it, and the finish held up well. While the slimmer design isn’t a major change, I found the new Colorsoft quite comfortable to hold compared to older Kindle devices.

For those who enjoy reading in the bath or by the pool, the Colorsoft is waterproof, so you don’t have to worry about accidental splashes or spills damaging the e-reader.

One thing I appreciated about the Colorsoft was how infrequently the screen needed to refresh, which was something I noticed more often with the larger Kindle Scribe Colorsoft . I also didn’t experience any noticeable ghosting, where text from previous pages lingers on the screen, which is common on some e-readers.

The Signature Edition supports a magnetic cover with built-in page-turn buttons that connects to the pogo pins on the back of the device, but I can’t speak to this experience because I didn’t have access to the case.

The biggest drawback of the Colorsoft is its price. It’s a steep investment for a device that’s just used for reading. That said, if you really want a color display, the Colorsoft is definitely worth considering. For everyone else, it’s a nice upgrade, but far from a must-have. Many readers would be better off with the basic Kindle or Paperwhite, which start at $169.99 and $199.99, respectively.

articles.title: Lakshmi Niwas completes 300 episodes, team celebrates the special milestone in a grand manner; Manasi Joshi Roy says 'Reaching 300 episodes is a wonderful milestone'
articles.summary: Lakshmi Niwas has been winning hearts of audiences across India ever since it went on air and now, it has reached yet another a significant milestone,
articles.body: Lakshmi Niwas has been winning hearts of audiences across India ever since it went on air and now, it has reached yet another a significant milestone, completing 300 episodes with a bang! Headlined by Manasi Joshi Roy as Lakshmi and Rajendra Chawla as Shriniwas, the show traces the journey of a couple who choose love over privilege and set out to build a life together, with the dream of owning a home of their own. Through their experiences, the show has brought to the forefront the aspirations, sacrifices and relationships that shape family life.Over the course of its journey, Lakshmi Niwas has seen its narrative evolve through changing family dynamics, generational differences and unexpected turns. While Lakshmi and Shriniwas continue to remain at the heart of the story, the lives and choices of those around them have introduced new conflicts and dimensions to the narrative. From navigating relationships within the family to dealing with situations that test their bonds, the show has explored how individual decisions can impact an entire family. A true reflection of several family situations across India, the family drama has struck a chord with the audience and been a hit across the country!The show has now completed 300 episodes, which was a very special moment for the cast and crew. They marked this occasion with a fun-filled celebration on the set with a cake cutting in the presence of friends, media and crew members. They also took an opportunity to acknowledge the viewers who have followed the show's journey and continued to be part of the family's many milestones.As Manasi Joshi Roy, who plays the role of Lakshmi, said, "Reaching 300 episodes is a wonderful milestone in our journey. When we began we knew that we were bringing a family and its relationships to the screen, but over time, these characters have become so much more familiar and personal to all of us. To play the titular role of Lakshmi has been extremely gratifying and I can say that today I’m not just playing the character of Lakshmi. She has become an intrinsic part of the actor in me. Her strength, her commitment to her family and the way she navigates the storms that life throws her way have made this journey very fulfilling for me. Every milestone is a reminder of the effort that goes into making a show, and I am happy to be celebrating this one with the entire team. Because at the end of the day it’s all a team effort and we do have a wonderful team from my producers to the director, and the lovely cast members who all have become friends. Here’s to many more episodes and many more milestones."Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Supriya Shukla on her role in Mannat 2: I knew my year-long wait was over when I read Jolly Juneja
articles.summary: Supriya Shukla, best known for playing Sarla Arora in Kumkum Bhagya and Kundali Bhagya, returned to television after a break of more than a year with
articles.body: Supriya Shukla, best known for playing Sarla Arora in Kumkum Bhagya and Kundali Bhagya, returned to television after a break of more than a year with Mannat – Har Khushi Paane Ki 2. The actress, who has also featured in shows such as Tere Liye, Molkki and Bade Achhe Lagte Hain 3, is currently seen as Jolly Juneja in her comeback show. The family drama also reunited her with familiar colleagues and draws on her experience of raising two daughters.Talking about what drew her to the project, Supriya says, “I was incredibly excited to return to television after more than a year away. For me, acting is all about waiting for a script with real depth. The moment I read the character of Jolly Juneja, I knew my wait was over. Jolly is a beautifully written, multi-layered woman.”The role also brings an interesting personal connection for the actress, as she plays a mother of four daughters on screen. She says, “In a fun twist, I am playing a mother to four daughters, which feels so natural since I raise two amazing daughters in real life.”The show brought Supriya back together with people she has shared a professional association with over the years. Expressing her gratitude to the team, she says, “The show reunited me with my long-time professional friends, whom I love and have enjoyed working with on several projects: producer Mukta Dhond and Jaspreet Saluja (Jassi). I am so grateful to them for trusting me with Jolly. We are working incredibly hard to take the beloved legacy of Mannat forward.”Before joining the cast of Mannat – Har Khushi Paane Ki 2, Supriya was associated with the Mumbai Independent Film Festival 2026 as a Grand Jury member. The experience gave her an opportunity to engage with independent cinema and encourage emerging talent. Recalling her involvement, she says, “Before stepping onto the sets of Mannat 2, I had the privilege of serving as a Grand Jury member at the Mumbai Independent Film Festival 2026. The festival has become a fantastic platform for original independent cinema.”She was also involved in the festival’s activities alongside its organising team, which included her husband, Haril Shukla, the festival chairman. Supriya says, “It was a joy to support this initiative led by my husband and Festival Chairman, Haril Shukla, alongside Festival Director Arhima Sharma and Creative Director Yoggesh Kumar Malhotra. We were also deeply honoured to welcome National Award-winning filmmaker Bharat Dilip Shitole and Kanupriya Shankar Pandit as our esteemed Guests of Honour.”The festival experience, she adds, gave her a fresh creative impetus just before beginning work on her new show. “Watching these exceptional independent projects and hosting an acting workshop for aspiring talent completely recharged my creative energy. I am stepping onto this new set inspired, motivated and ready to deliver a performance you will love,” she concludes.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.
